cases.customer_question: If TCRL updates add new mandatory HOGP test cases after initial testing, must all testing be rerun or can only the additional test cases be executed?
question_variants: Do TCRL-added tests require complete retesting?
Can additional HOGP test cases be submitted separately?
Must PTS reports be regenerated as one file?
How should late-added TCRL test cases be handled?
Can incremental Bluetooth test evidence be submitted?
cases.actual_issue: A future TCRL release announced additional mandatory HOGP test cases effective after a specific date, raising concern about whether all prior testing had to be repeated.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The customer had already completed most Bluetooth profile testing before new mandatory tests were announced in a future TCRL release. They wanted to avoid rerunning all tests unnecessarily. The consultant clarified that only the new additional tests needed to be executed and documented separately.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant reviewed the existing HOGP and ScPP reports against the generated test plan and confirmed that the current evidence was sufficient for registrations before the future TCRL activation date. For registrations after the effective date, ten additional HOGP test cases would need to be added. The consultant clarified that the HSP report did not need to be regenerated as a single combined report and that the additional test cases could be executed separately and submitted as an additional report package.
cases.decision_logic: Qualification evidence requirements are tied to the active TCRL version and effective date. Previously executed valid tests remain usable, while only newly introduced mandatory test cases must be added for later submissions.
cases.final_recommendation: Reuse the existing valid PTS evidence and execute only the newly added mandatory HOGP test cases if qualification occurs after the new TCRL activation date. Submit the added results as supplemental reports.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: If the new mandatory test cases are omitted after the TCRL effective date, the qualification submission may fail review or require resubmission. Repeating all testing unnecessarily can also increase schedule and cost.
